findings.summary: The production `spawnRole` dep can never return a body, so the generate stage can never complete from the production entry. The default runtime's `readBody` looks up `findWorkerResult(runId, runsMessages)`, but `runsMessages` is the `board:agent-runs` snapshot read at src/tick-run.ts:1292 — before any generate role is spawned — while `runId` is a fresh `randomUUID()` created at src/tick-run.ts:1470. A result for that run id can never be present in that pre-spawn array (it is a plain array, never re-read and never mutated), so `readBody` deterministically falls through and throws `generate role <role> result not found for run <runId>`. Production never injects `opts.generateDeps` (parseRunCliArgs/RunCliOptions has no such field; tick-entry.ts:147-148 passes only parsed CLI options), so every real invocation aborts inside the first `Promise.all` debater spawn: no argument docs, no report doc, no export. spec §1.2 requires a real production implementation for `spawnRole`/`spawnRuntime`, and spec §0's products 1 and 2 therefore still cannot be produced. Unlike the sibling harvest path (src/tick-run.ts:1355), which legitimately reads results of runs spawned in earlier ticks, the generate path spawns and reads back inside one call and needs a fresh read (tick-inspect.ts:271 `readWorkerResult` exists and re-reads). No test covers this: U1/U2/U4 all inject `generateDeps.spawnRole`, and generate.test.ts:379 injects its own `spawnRuntime.readBody`.

The one-shot guarantee marks the origin as generated *before* the generate stage runs and never rolls it back on failure, converting the loud failure the spec demands into the forbidden permanent silent skip. `markGeneratedInAnyProcess(origin)` runs at src/tick-run.ts:1450, while `await runGenerate(...)` is only reached at src/tick-run.ts:1529 with no try/catch/rollback. Any throw inside runGenerate — the always-throwing production `spawnRole` above, `MissingExportRootError` (src/tick-run.ts:1499), or a bus publish failure — leaves the tmp marker on disk. The first tick fails loudly (tick-entry.ts:151-155 exits 2), the fleet routes the claim back to `open` (fleet.yaml.tpl:27-29), and every subsequent tick then finds the marker, reports `generateTriggered:false` and exits 0, so the report and the export are permanently lost with no signal. This directly contradicts spec §1.3 (`⛔ EXPORT_ROOT 未配置 ⇒ 响亮失败，不得静默跳过导出（静默跳过 = 产物 2 消失且没人知道）`). The package's own U4 negative case (test/g4c-generate-wiring.test.ts:324-351) exercises exactly this sequence — marker written, then MissingExportRootError — without asserting anything about the poisoned retry.

U2 has zero discriminating power over the cross-process half of the one-shot mechanism, i.e. over exactly the property the previous Final review rejected. The test drives two `runChannelWrite` calls inside one process; `hasGeneratedInAnyProcess` (src/tick-run.ts:376-379) checks the module-level `generatedOrigins` Set first, and that Set is still populated from the first call, so the `existsSync(oneShotMarkerPath(origin))` branch never decides anything. Deleting the file-marker read and write entirely (reverting to the previously rejected in-memory-only mechanism) leaves U2 and mutation T2 green. Spec U2 requires a 判别性用例 for 「同一次研究的终态被**连续两个 tick**观察到」, and in production each tick is a fresh process (tick.md:81 invokes `"$tick_entry" --run`; bin/tick-entry.sh:8 `exec node .../vite-node`). The exported `resetGeneratedOrigins()` (src/tick-run.ts:356-358) clears only the Set and would have let the test model a fresh tick process between the two calls, but it is used only in `beforeEach`. The dev-note's claim 「跨进程持久由文件标记保证」 is therefore asserted by nothing.

Mutation T4 is zero-power against the only `spawnAnchorCheck` implementation this package authored. The production default at src/tick-run.ts:1494-1495 (`async () => { throw new AnchorCheckNotWiredError(); }`) is never exercised: every test that reaches runGenerate through `runChannelWrite` explicitly injects `spawnAnchorCheck: async () => { throw new AnchorCheckNotWiredError(); }` (test/g4c-generate-wiring.test.ts:144, 171, 214, 344), and the U5 cases (test/g4c-generate-wiring.test.ts:374-443) build their own `GenerateDeps` with their own throwing stub. Replacing the production default with `{defects: 0, verificationRate: 0}` — spec §3 T4, whose expected outcome is `U5 必须挂` — therefore kills no assertion, so the §1.4 requirement that this package's `spawnAnchorCheck` throw a distinctive loud error is unguarded.

The production `lockSynthesizer` is a no-op stub, not the singleton lock spec §1.2 requires. It returns a per-call closure whose release only flips a local `released` boolean; it acquires nothing, waits for nothing and excludes nothing, so `synthesizer 并发 = 1` (spec §1.2 table, and the semantics pinned in the GenerateDeps doc comment at src/generate.ts:344-349) holds only accidentally because each tick process runs runGenerate at most once. spec §1.2 demands a production implementation for each of the ten deps and explicitly names this one 「单例 lock，wait-then-run」; the deployment already documents an available named-lock primitive (bin/deep-research-loop.sh:9-11). U6's ordering assertions (test/g4c-generate-wiring.test.ts:501-528) inject their own lock, so nothing covers the production stub either.

The production `writeDoc` silently defaults the research.doc.v2 destination to the clue board channel, and no production assembly layer ever passes `--doc-channel` — the same 「CLI 支持它、引擎依赖它、唯独生产从不传它」 shape that caused the previous rejection for `--origin`. `const channelId = opts.docChannelId ?? opts.channelId` sends report/argument docs to e.g. `research:v1-deep-research.index`, while the code's own comment at src/tick-run.ts:1020 says production must point at a content channel (src/export.ts:4 documents 「报告落 doc(report) 进 research:content」). `--doc-channel` appears only in the parser (src/tick-run.ts:1732-1737) and the usage text (src/tick-entry.ts:42); fleet.yaml.tpl, workflow.yaml, tick.md and bin/deep-research-loop.sh never supply it. Bus writes are append-only with no DELETE, and this repo's established discipline forbids exactly this kind of silent channel default (bin/deep-research-loop.sh:105-110).

The one-shot marker lives in a machine-global, never-expiring namespace keyed only on the origin, while the default origin is a deterministic sha256 of RESEARCH_QUESTION (`RESEARCH_ORIGIN="dr-$(printf '%s' "$RESEARCH_QUESTION" | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)"`, bin/deep-research-loop.sh:99-102). Consequently a later, legitimately separate research run on the same question resolves to the same `${tmpdir()}/g4c-generated-<origin>.marker`, finds the stale marker from the earlier run, and silently skips the whole generate stage (`generateTriggered:false`, exit 0) — no report, no export, no signal. The marker is scoped neither to the run root (`RUN_ROOT`, bin/deep-research-loop.sh:68) nor to any completion state, and the surrounding comment at bin/deep-research-loop.sh:97-98 asserts 「⛔ 无内置缺省」 immediately before providing exactly a built-in derived default.

The dev-note fails several U8/U9/U10 evidence requirements that spec §2 declares 硬验收（缺一不可）. U8 requires 「贴基线与终值」 with the baseline measured on G4b-merged main, but only a 终值 column exists (22 files / 274 cases) with no baseline; the same table states 「失败 | 0」 and then 「4 例预存环境失败」 in the same cell, which is self-contradictory and in any case not the 全绿 U8 demands. The 硬验收逐条 table covers only U1–U7 — U8, U9 and U10 have no rows. The §3 mutation matrix reports predictions rather than measurements: the T3 and T4 「实测」 cells merely restate what the assertion checks and never state that the mutation was applied and observed to fail; no row 回显被改行 as §3 requires; and the T1 cell claims 「去掉 runGenerate 调用 ⇒ generateTriggered 保持 false」, which is contradicted by src/tick-run.ts:1451 setting `generateTriggered = true` before the call (T1 is in fact killed only by the spy assertions). The 还原证据 says `git status --porcelain` 「仅在上述交付物文件有改动」, which is not the 「为空」 U9 requires.

The production export wiring violates an explicit ⛔ constraint of the module spec §1.3 told it to reuse: `createdAt: new Date().toISOString()` takes the current system clock, while `ExportInput.createdAt` is documented as 「bus 消息的 created_at —— 文件名日期由此派生，不得现取系统时钟」 (src/export.ts:22-23) and src/export.ts:10-12 requires 同一输入 ⇒ 同一字节. `deriveExportPath` slices this value for the filename date (src/export.ts:54), so the export path is no longer a deterministic function of the report data. `publishDoc` returns only `{message_id, channel_seq}` (src/bus.ts:72-76), so the bus `created_at` was never plumbed through the widened `writeDoc` contract.

No test locks the newly added `--origin` production assembly chain, so the exact wiring hole that caused the previous Final rejection has no regression guard. `--origin` appears in tests only as a `parseRunCliArgs` unit case (test/g4c-generate-wiring.test.ts:581-593) and as programmatic `origin:` options; nothing asserts `research_origin` in fleet.yaml.tpl:16, workflow.yaml:27, or that tick.md:51 actually appends `--origin <value>` to the tick-entry argv. The sibling G4a package established precisely that assertion pattern (test/g4a-question-wiring.test.ts:92-143 renders tick.md against an argv-recording fake tick-entry and checks fleet input against the profile value), and the G4a Q4 flag matrix (test/g4a-question-wiring.test.ts:183-212) does not cover `--origin` either. Deleting tick.md:51 or fleet.yaml.tpl:16 would keep the suite green.

Identity preconditions hold on the controller-supplied values: input_commit, expected_remote_head and subject_commit are all 36b651d33464242cc6dd6ad89c9562ca60ff73c5, and implementation_subject_commit 5ab2a04494aaf75ab44d0f66ed18921aab5ad1cb is distinct from it; the deterministic seal verifies the actual Git HEAD. The spec at .dev-dispatch/spec/approved.md and all four feedback-index artifacts were read, including the Continuous verdict for this attempt (.dev-dispatch/reviews/rc-attempt_01KZK92NX9TWSV06GRNB5VXZTM/review.json, APPROVE, no findings) and the prior Final REJECT (.dev-dispatch/reviews/rf-attempt_01KZK7WW6MZE3RY1604ADE2XK2/review.json). Both of that review's blockers are materially addressed — `--origin` now flows bin → fleet → workflow → tick.md, and the one-shot guarantee now has a cross-process file marker — and U1's positive/negative pair through runChannelWrite (converged via prevZeroGrowthRounds=2 vs null via 0/0) is genuinely discriminating and does kill T1. This Final judgment is reached independently of the Continuous verdict.
